title: GPT Image 2.6 Flare
summary: Generate image with GPT Image 2.6 Flare
description: OpenAI GPT Image 2.6 Flare — the fast GPT Image model, for everyday images and quick edits with sharp text. Text-to-image, and editing or combining up to 16 reference images; transparent backgrounds; output up to 4K. New in 2.6: complexity sets how much the model plans before it renders. Billing: per output image by quality, the same at every size and with any number of references — low 70, medium 120, high 175, xhigh 340, max 675 credits. Default quality medium (120 credits).

background.description: Output background. transparent returns a cut-out with a transparent background, from text or an edit (as PNG, or WebP if asked: JPEG has no transparency). auto lets the model decide.

complexity.description: How much the model plans before it renders. high suits dense text, complex layouts and scenes where objects relate to each other; medium and low plan less, are faster, and suit focused edits such as changing a background or a sign. Does not change the price.

prompt.description: Text description of the image to generate. Write `@handle` to cast a character: a BudgetPixel AI influencer or one of your own ([`GET /v1/characters`](/api-reference/characters/list-characters-you-can-cast)).

quality.description: Rendering detail. Per image, at any size: low 70, medium 120, high 175, xhigh 340, max 675 credits.

reference_images.description: Optional reference images (up to 16) to edit or combine into one image. Each item is a public image URL, a data URI, raw base64, or an uploaded-file URL from POST /v1/uploads. Omit for text-to-image. References do not change the price.

resolution.description: Output size tier; the price is the same at every size. 1:1 renders 1024x1024 at 1K and 2048x2048 at 2K or 4K. 16:9 and 9:16 render 2048x1152 / 1152x2048 at 1K or 2K, and 3840x2160 / 2160x3840 at 4K. 3:2, 2:3, 4:3 and 3:4 have one size each (1536x1024, 1024x1536, 1536x1152, 1152x1536). With aspect_ratio auto the model picks the size, and an edit keeps its input's shape.
